 Manchester United came from two goals down – twice – to salvage a 4-4 draw with Aston Villa at Old Trafford

 2h ago GOAL!! United 2-3 Villa (McGinn pen 48) 
 2h ago Penalty to Villa!

 32m ago 14.02 EST Jamie Jackson has filed his match report, so that’s my cue to get some fresh air. One last fact: this seven-game winless run in the league is not United’s worst ever. In fact it’s not even the worst in the past two years: towards the end of the dismal 2024-25 season, Ruben Amorim’s team went eight games without a win.
 Thanks for your company, correspondence and thoughts on Thing 1 and Thing 2.
 Dorgu rescues point for Manchester United in eight-goal thriller against Aston Villa Read more Share Updated at  14.14 EST 40m ago 13.54 EST Somewhere in all that mayhem, Patrick Dorgu came on for his first minutes in ages and grabbed an assist and a goal. And now he’s being asked to say how he feels.
 “I don’t feel happy,” he says. “We’re in a bad situation… We had lots of opportunities and we should have won this game.”
 Share 44m ago 13.51 EST The stats are in, and they seem to be saying that the better side was … United. They beat Villa 26-12 on shots, 9-6 on shots on target, 3.55-2.88 on expected goals, 44-18 on touches in the opposition box and 30-5 on crosses. But, to be fair, they also won 2-1 on hapless episodes in their own box, and 2-0 on ridiculous starts to a half.
 Share 47m ago 13.48 EST “Thing 1 and Thing 2” is the subject line of the next email. “What would it take,” asks Michael Meagher, “to get rid of Wilcox & Berrada? Mystifying that they still have their jobs.”
 Share 50m ago 13.44 EST “There’s probably a delicious irony,” says Kevin Wilson, “in that Lindelof was pretty ordinary during his Man Utd career but would still be the best defender if he was still in the Utd line up.”
 Share 52m ago 13.42 EST “Evening Tim,” says Simon McMahon. “Is relegation the logical and inevitable conclusion to the post-Fergie years at Old Trafford? I don’t know, but it feels like something has to happen, either at managerial or board level...”
 Share 54m ago 13.40 EST Here’s another email, in its entirety. “Hello Tim. Football, bloody silly. Best wishes, Kári Tulinius.”
 Share Updated at  13.41 EST 55m ago 13.39 EST A glance at the inbox. “Emery,” says John Delaney, “ putting out a good advert that he’s got what it takes to be a United manager!”
 Share 1h ago 13.38 EST Unai Emery seems to have stormed down the tunnel. Sky are looking at whether, in the melee at the corner, Suzuki was fouled – by his opposite number, Senne Lammens, who may have backed into him. The consensus is no.
 Share Updated at  13.38 EST 1h ago 13.37 EST Where does that leave us? United rise from 19th to 18th, edging out Sunderland on goal difference. Villa sneak up to 10th, above Spurs and Newcastle.
 It’s a funny old table. You can be eighth with three wins out of 10, as Brentford are. You can be 13th with only two wins, as Hull are. You can be any of the promoted sides and spend this international break sitting above the once-mighty Man United.
 Share 1h ago 13.34 EST The players are now wandering around looking daxed and confused, as well they may. Carrick, calm as ever, applauds the crowd and his men join him. It sounds as if the fans are singing Carrick’s name.
 Share 1h ago 13.32 EST Sorry not to have had a moment to look at the mail. On the plus side, if you wrote in when United were two goals down as they were for most of this match, at least you are spared any embarrassment regarding hostages to fortune.
 Share 1h ago 13.30 EST FULL TIME! Man United 4-4 Villa
 It is 40 years to the day since Alex Ferguson took over at United. And they have just scored twice in Fergie time to salvage a draw. Football, bloody hell.
 View image in fullscreen Manchester United manager Michael Carrick with Leny Yoro after the final whistle. Photograph: Martin Rickett/PA Share Updated at  13.38 EST 1h ago 13.28 EST 90+7 min The biggest roar of the night goes to the VAR, who confirmed the equaliser.
 Share 1h ago 13.28 EST GOAL!!! Man United 4-4 Villa (Dorgu? 90+6)
 They’ve got one of the two! Suzuki messes up a corner and Dorgu nods the ball home.
 View image in fullscreen Manchester United’s Patrick Dorgu scores their fourth goal. Photograph: Jon Super/Reuters View image in fullscreen Dorgu runs off to celebrate. Photograph: Catherine Ivill/AMA/Getty Images Share Updated at  13.36 EST 1h ago 13.26 EST 90+5 min United have one minute to get two goals. It’s not going to happen.
 Share 1h ago 13.25 EST 90+3 min Cunha goes down in the box … no pen! And then a loose ball comes out to Mount, who slices his half-volley. Omar Berrada throws up his hands in a rare show of emotion.
 Share Updated at  13.26 EST 1h ago 13.24 EST 90+3 min United pile forward again. Fernandes to Mount, who tries a one-two but sells his captain short.
 Share 1h ago 13.23 EST GOAL! Man United 3-4 Villa (Zirkzee 90+2)
 Ooh! A simple cross from Dorgu, a simple finish for Zirkzee. The last throw of the dice has worked.
 View image in fullscreen Joshua Zirkzee of Manchester United scores his team’s third goal. Photograph: Michael Regan/Getty Images View image in fullscreen Zirkzee celebrates scoring to make it 3-4. Photograph: Paul Currie/Shutterstock Share Updated at  13.31 EST 1h ago 13.21 EST 90 min Fernandes tries to slip the ball in behinf fopr Mainoo, who has run out of puff. He’s been better than most in red shirts.
 Share 1h ago 13.20 EST 87 min United hit the bar! It’s Mount, timing his run like Frank Lampard and doing well to help Fernandes’ chip on its way.
 Share 1h ago 13.19 EST 87 min Lacey sends in a cross that is overhit. Behind the dotted line Carrick is pensive, Emery animated. I suspect the home crowd, fond as they are of Carrick, would now be happy to see Emery take his place.
 Share 1h ago 13.17 EST 87 min Unai Emery sends on his fifth sub, Madjo for Jackson. Barkley gets a shot away, saved by Lammens.
 Share 1h ago 13.17 EST 85 min Mount gives the ball away to Mbaye, who spares his blushes by returning the favour.
 Share 1h ago 13.15 EST 84 min Fernandes should be running the show, but it’s actually Ross Barkley. He sends a fine through ball down the right, where Dorgu has to pull off a sliding tackle.
 Share 1h ago 13.14 EST 83 min Michael Carrick decides it’s time for one last throw of the dice. He removes Mbeumo, who has been tireless but toothless, and sends on Joshua Zirkzee, who would be an unlikely saviour.
 Share 1h ago 13.13 EST 82 min A few United fans are trickling out. The rest are still making plenty of noise, but it feels as if they’re amusing themselves rather than rousing the troops for another famous fightback.
 Share 1h ago 13.12 EST 80 min Fernandes sends a through ball to Dorgu, who is too rusty to control it.
 Share 1h ago 13.10 EST 79 min Villa knock the ball around, which is all they have to do now to secure their fourth league win at Old Trafford in 70 years.
 Share 1h ago 13.09 EST 78 min Two more Villa subs, both alliterative: Mbaye for Manzambi, Gomes for Goretzka.
 Share 1h ago 13.08 EST 76 min Lacey wins a corner, which leads to another. Eventually there’s a half-chance for Mbeumo, who sends it wide.
 Share 1h ago 13.06 EST 75 min United’s passing has become disjointed, not that this is their biggest problem.
 Share 2h ago 13.04 EST 72 min … and another: Alysson off, Ross Barkley on. So three goalscorers have now left the stage.
 Share 2h ago 13.03 EST 71 min Villa sub: McGinn, after playing well and getting an assist as well as a penalty, gives way to George Hemmings…
 Share Updated at  13.03 EST 2h ago 13.02 EST 71 min A box shows that United have now conceded 30 goals this season, making them joint top of the Leakiest Defence League – in Europe. They share this dubious honour with Palace and Sassuolo.
 Share 2h ago 13.01 EST 70 min Cunha gets a shot on target, and then Fernandes finds Row Z.
 Share 2h ago 13.00 EST 69 min Lacey gives the ball away near the half-way line and concedes a free kick as he tries to make amends.
 Share 2h ago 12.58 EST 67 min Lacey has already sent in a cross. A moment later, Mbeumo slides a shot past the near post.
 Share 2h ago 12.57 EST 66 min Here come the subs, as advertised. Off go Tielemans (who scored), Dalot (who had, sad to say, a shocker) and Amad (who was better than the other night).
 Share 2h ago 12.56 EST 64 min Carrick, who has nothing to lose now, is preparing three subs: Mount, Dorgu and Lacey.
 Share Updated at  12.56 EST 2h ago 12.54 EST 62 min Fernandes plays a square pass to Cunha, whose shot goes wide. There seems to have been a deflection as it brings a corner, which comes to nowt.
 Share 2h ago 12.53 EST 61 min Amad wins a free kick off Goretzka. A chance for Fernandes to get a rare assist?
 Share 2h ago 12.52 EST 60 min A United attack, patient by the standards of this crazy match, leads to another left-foot shot from Tielemans, not nearly as good as the one that supplied the equaliser.
 Share 2h ago 12.51 EST 60 min United, who had crept up to 18th, are now 19th again, saved from the bottom only by their goal difference. It’s bad (-7), but only half as bad as Palace’s (-14).
 Share 2h ago 12.50 EST 57 min Mbeumo, slipped in by Cunha, gets a shot on target but (a) it’s easily saved and (b) the flag is up.
 Share 2h ago 12.48 EST 56 min Tielemans, who was so good for half an hour, now plays a hospital pass and the upshot is that Heaven goes into the book for stopping a quick break.
 Share Updated at  12.48 EST 2h ago 12.47 EST 55 min Carrick, seeing that, bowed his head and pinched the furrow between his eyes, as if he couldn’t believe them.
 Share 2h ago 12.45 EST GOAL! Man United 2-4 Villa (Goretzka 53)
 You couldn’t make it up. Yoro almost heads into his own net, there’s a goalmouth scramble, Goretzka keeps calm and puts it away. And once again, United have conceded two at the start of a half.
 View image in fullscreen Aston Villa's Leon Goretzka (L) shoots to score the team's fourth goal. Photograph: Darren Staples/AFP/Getty Images Share Updated at  13.05 EST 2h ago 12.43 EST 52 min McGinn wins a free kick off Fernandes, whose reaction you may just be able to guess.
 Share 2h ago 12.41 EST 51 min Mazraoui gets away down the right, only to send his cross curling out for a goal kick.
 Share 2h ago 12.40 EST 50 min That wasn’t in the script. But it was on brand for poor Dalot.
 Share 2h ago 12.39 EST GOAL!! United 2-3 Villa (McGinn pen 48)
 John McGinn slams it in, and yet again United have started a half badly.
 View image in fullscreen John McGinn of Aston Villa scores. Photograph: Conor Molloy/ProSports/Shutterstock Share Updated at  12.48 EST 2h ago 12.38 EST Penalty to Villa!
 Dalot lunges at Alysson, who goes down – and the whistle goes. It’s unlikely to be overturned.
 View image in fullscreen Alysson Edward of Aston Villa is fouled by Diogo Dalot of Manchester United resulting in a penalty. Photograph: Carl Recine/Getty Images Share Updated at  13.09 EST 2h ago 12.36 EST 46 min United sub: Maguire is off, presumed injured. Ayden Heaven is on – not the more experienced Matthijs de Ligt.
